headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared file/API workflows; no direct evidence of a shared channel, so interaction is inferred.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee can ingest documents and session memory, while plano exposes config.yaml and an OpenAI-compatible API path. A direct shared channel is not documented, but if plano forwards cognee-produced content into prompts or files, instruction-like content could be reinterpreted. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF plano reads cognee-generated documents or summaries into prompts without sanitization, injection risk is active.
IF a shared workspace or config file is used as a bridge, attacker-controlled text can cross agents.
mitigations: Add a prompt-delimiter wrapper around all cognee outputs before plano consumes them.
Review any file handoff path for instruction-like text and strip control tokens.
Use separate directories for cognee and plano artifacts.
Log and reject unexpected role markers in imported content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every cross-agent payload.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents; plano has broad network egress and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. No shared filesystem is documented, but if either agent forwards shared artifacts to its backend, sensitive data can leave the local boundary. The pairwise path is inferred, not proven.
conditions: IF cognee exports customer-support or finance documents into plano prompts, those data may be transmitted off-box.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, file contents can be exposed through plano's API calls.
mitigations: Keep sensitive cognee datasets out of any plano-ingested directory.
Disable or restrict plano egress for runs that touch personal or finance data.
Use separate API keys and tenants for each agent.
Inspect outbound requests for document payloads before enabling production traffic.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances and session-scoped memory, while plano does not support multiple instances and uses an out-of-process dataplane. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface, so a write-write conflict is not established. The remaining risk is limited to unusual orchestration mistakes.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same config or state directory, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator reuses one mutable resource across sessions, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories to each agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared config.yaml files.
Serialize updates through one orchestrator process.
Check for lock files before writing shared state.
requires-engineering: add explicit resource locking around mutable stores.

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, while plano is a gateway that can route or forward model calls. If plano treats cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated guidance into downstream actions. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF plano forwards cognee-generated recommendations without validation, incorrect guidance can propagate.
IF cognee outputs are used as routing policy or tool instructions, downstream actions may follow bad assumptions.
mitigations: Require a human review step before acting on cognee outputs.
Add schema validation to any cognee-to-plano handoff.
Compare outputs against a second source before execution.
Reject free-form instructions where structured fields are expected.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while plano exposes logs, traces, and metrics. If the pair is used on regulated customer-support data, retention or residency mismatches can arise, especially because plano's broad egress and logging surfaces are documented. The other agent is cited because the compliance issue is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated customer-support or finance data is routed through plano logs or traces, retention obligations may be violated.
IF the deployment requires data residency controls and plano egress is unrestricted, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Exclude regulated fields from plano logs and traces.
Set short retention on any shared telemetry.
Route only de-identified payloads through plano.
Document the data flow for support and finance records.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls.
